# Noisy-release boundaries: an analytic obstruction and a charged energy test

1 November2026. Two internally reviewed boundary results. Neither invalidates the accepted ideal thermal encoder or the equilibrium-initialized static-H memory theorem.

## 1. A tempting quantum inverse-noise proof route fails
The explicit bounded-degree three-local chain in operator_log/ has a nonremovable operator-log derivative pole at complex weak coupling of order1/n. Thus a volume-uniform JOINT ANALYTIC/Taylor–Cauchy expansion for the inverse-Pauli Gibbs Hamiltonian is false, even in this special local family.

This does NOT prove that real-axis locality, an efficient nonanalytic preparer, or noisy release is impossible. The finite operator-polymer positivity result remains valid. Positivity was not enough to justify the proposed operator-log algorithm; the failed inference is now explicitly ruled out rather than silently assumed.

Read operator_log/EXACT_COMPLEX_POLE_BARRIER.md and its independent receipt. Numerical identities/countertests are corroboration of the exact proof.

A polynomial-probability clean thermal workspace branch supplies a logical error path. The separately reviewed amplification uses independent fresh resource banks and a random logical Pauli to turn successful reduced-memory branches into entanglement-breaking channels. After polynomially many attempts, Bell infidelity is at least3/8-o(1).
